question: What provenance and locality context does Herre's 1923 eel review report for the historical Fowler eel entry?

sourceScan.title: A Review of the Eels of the Philippine Archipelago
sourceScan.author: Albert W. C. T. Herre
sourceScan.scanSource: University of Michigan volume scan distributed through Internet Archive and Wikimedia Commons.

retrievalAssessment.textAccess: Search-indexed OCR excerpt attributed to printed page 125 was available and reviewed. The source PDF is an 824-page, approximately 25.8 MB volume; the browser retrieval tool could not open the PDF because of its content-size limit.
retrievalAssessment.ocrCaveat: OCR may misread historical taxon spellings, punctuation, and line breaks. The page image and full article were not visually checked, so the excerpt is provisional text evidence only.

findings.statement: The page-125 OCR says Herre had not personally seen specimens from the Philippines and that the species was recorded by Fowler.
findings.evidenceType: Search-indexed OCR excerpt from a scan of Herre's 1923 article.

findings.statement: Herre reports that the Fowler specimen was held by the Philadelphia Commercial Museum and was labeled only at the Philippine Islands level; the excerpt gives no more specific locality.
findings.evidenceType: Search-indexed OCR excerpt from Herre, not a direct reading of Fowler's article or the specimen label.

findings.statement: The OCR excerpt's footnote identifies Fowler's Copeia no. 58 report, dated 18 June 1918, page 62.
findings.evidenceType: Search-indexed OCR excerpt from Herre's article.

findings.statement: The OCR places the account under the historical name Fluta alba; this is a historical usage, not a verified modern identification of the specimen or a present-day Philippine population.
findings.evidenceType: Search-indexed OCR excerpt; spelling has not been checked against the page image.

evidenceLimits.locality: ‘Philippine Islands’ is an island-level label, not a verified NCR, Pasig, Cavite, waterbody, or collection-site locality.
evidenceLimits.collectionAndIntroductionDates: The excerpt supplies no collection date or arrival/introduction date. The 1918 citation year is a publication date, not an introduction date.
evidenceLimits.specimenIdentity: No catalog number or accession identifier is given in the excerpt. It does not link the Philadelphia Commercial Museum specimen to the 14 Smithsonian lots USNM 135196–135209 reviewed separately.
evidenceLimits.taxonomy: The historical name Fluta alba and Herre's account do not establish the modern identity or native/introduced status of a particular specimen or population.
evidenceLimits.sourceRelationship: This is a 1923 secondary account of Fowler's report; the original Fowler page and the original specimen label remain unreviewed.

evidenceDecision.decision: Retain this as provisional historical source-chain context: by 1923, Herre described Fowler's eel report as based on a specimen with only a broad Philippine Islands label. Do not convert it into a waterbody occurrence, a Pasig/NCR record, an introduction date, or a confirmed modern taxon.

nextActions: Continue looking for a permitted readable copy of Fowler page 62; do not bypass repository access controls.
Search Philadelphia Commercial Museum archival catalogs for a specimen identifier that could be checked against the Smithsonian catalog, without assuming the records are the same.
Continue the 1989 national introduction-history source-chain review and keep all dates, specimens, waterbodies, and taxonomic identities separate.
